result:
Yes — this breaks the property you just built the gate for. If the formatter commits *after* approval but *before* merge, the code that actually ships is no longer the code whose hash you recorded as approved; "we can point to exactly what was signed off on" stops being true the moment gofmt/goimports touches the branch. goimports also isn't purely cosmetic (it edits import lists), so it's not obviously safe to wave through as a non-approval-worthy change either.

Two clean options: (1) run the formatter *before* the approval step, so the hash that gets approved is the hash that merges, or (2) if formatting must happen post-approval, treat the resulting commit as unapproved and re-trigger the gate (or store the post-format hash and explicitly note in the trace that formatting was auto-applied after sign-off, if your audit requirements tolerate that). Given you're citing this for release attestation, I'd push for option 1 — it's the same two-line hook, just moved earlier in the pipeline, and it preserves the "hash approved == hash merged" invariant with no tradeoff. "Marcus tried it and tests passed" doesn't validate the audit-integrity property, since nothing in CI would have caught this.
